title: Invocation 3-tuple type alias locks API shape and pins to serde_json major version
description:
crate-jmap-types/src/wire.rs:10 declares `pub type Invocation = (String, serde_json::Value, String)`.

Once shipped at 0.1.1, this 3-tuple shape is locked into the public API
for the entire `jmap-*` family. Two concrete cost paths for callers:

1. **Positional access locks the contract.** Every consumer (kith, stoa,
   the 7+ extension crates, third-party JMAP clients) writes
   `inv.0`, `inv.1`, `inv.2` to pull out method name, arguments, and
   call id. There is no rustdoc-hover assistance: the field positions
   are documented in prose on the alias but not on the values. Once
   downstream code ships, the maintainer cannot replace `Invocation`
   with a struct with named fields without a major-version break.

2. **`serde_json::Value` in the middle slot pins the crate's public API
   to serde_json's major version forever.** If serde_json 2.x ever ships
   with a renamed/reshaped `Value`, `Invocation` breaks transitively for
   every consumer. The contract committed in 0.1.1 is implicitly:
   \"`jmap-types` ^0.1 requires serde_json ^1\". A reasonable mitigation
   would be a newtype like `pub struct Invocation { name, args, call_id }`
   where `args` is `serde_json::Value` for now but could be wrapped or
   typed in a future minor without changing the outer shape.

A caller depending on this API in production accepts: (a) `inv.N`
positional access for the lifetime of `jmap-types ^0.1`; (b) recompile
when serde_json's major version moves; (c) no rustdoc-hover help on what
position 1 vs 2 means.

Fix candidates (any of which is a breaking change requiring a major
bump and so is the wrong way around — file now while still 0.x):
- Convert to `pub struct Invocation { pub name: String, pub args:
  serde_json::Value, pub call_id: String }` with `#[serde(into = "..."`
  / `from = "..."` to keep the 3-element-array wire form.
- Or accept the lock and add `Invocation::name()`, `args()`,
  `call_id()` accessor methods so callers can opt out of positional
  access (and `inv.0`-using callers stay buildable forever).
notes:
DECISION NEEDED (triage 2026-10-19 at 9fdbbbcf): Question for Mark: should Invocation stay a public 3-tuple alias with serde_json::Value in the middle, permanently, or become a named struct before the next 0.x release?

Options:
(A) Accept the lock. Keep the alias. Add an AGENTS.md paragraph saying that `(String, serde_json::Value, String)` is a deliberate commitment for jmap-types 0.x/1.x: it pins consumers to serde_json 1.x and to .0=method, .1=args, .2=call_id (RFC 8620 §3.2). Close JMAP-wlip.30 as a duplicate under the same decision. Size S, not breaking.
(B) Convert to `#[non_exhaustive]`-free `pub struct Invocation { pub name: String, pub arguments: serde_json::Value, pub call_id: String }` with a hand-written Serialize/Deserialize that keeps the 3-element JSON array wire form. Add `From<(String, Value, String)>` and `Into` the tuple to ease migration. Migrate all ~290 sites in 18 crates. Wire tests use RFC 8620 §3.3.1/§3.4.1 example request/response JSON as the oracle. Bump jmap-types to 0.3. Close JMAP-wlip.30 and settle JMAP-jfia.19 in the same pass. Size L, breaking.
(C) Do B, and also make args opaque (a newtype over Value) to remove the serde_json major pin. Rejected: JMAP-6xs8.18 (`extra: serde_json::Map`) and AGENTS.md's sloppy-Value policy already tie the public API to serde_json in many places, so decoupling Invocation alone buys nothing.

Recommendation: (B) without (C), done now while the crate is 0.2. The serde_json pin is already a workspace-wide fact, so accept it explicitly in AGENTS.md either way. The positional-tuple problem is the one that is cheap to fix now and expensive after 1.0. If Mark does not want a 290-site migration, choose (A) and record it as a bd decision so JMAP-wlip.30 and JMAP-jfia.19 can be closed against it.
DECIDED by Mark 2026-10-19: option B without C. Invocation becomes pub struct { name: String, arguments: serde_json::Value, call_id: String } with hand-written Serialize/Deserialize keeping the RFC 8620 3-element array wire form, plus From/Into (String, Value, String). Migrate all sites; ships in 0.3.0 (breaking). Oracle: RFC 8620 §3.3.1/§3.4.1 example JSON. Close JMAP-wlip.30 under this decision.
close_reason: Landed as df8926be (Invocation named struct, RFC 8620 array wire form kept). Review passed. CI green at 8e240e18 (stable+beta 3502 passed).
